content: What is the reason behind basing String.hash on MurmurHash2 rather than going for one which is cryptographically secure?

String.hash is supposed to be used for HashMap applications (like all the other hash functions you will see in core and most of the eco system). In order to qualify for a HashMap application there is no need to be cryptographically secure and other factors like speed of computation become much more interesting.

Ok, many thanks. Just a quick follow on question (out of curiosity more than anything else): In what sense does it not need to be cryptographically secure? In the strong sense that if someone constructed a collision of hashes nothing would go wrong, or in the weaker sense, that a collision of hashes would lead to something going wrong but it is nothing 'security critical', so it doesn't really matter.

Hash collisions are acceptable and handled in all data structures that make use of these hash functions. However, you do want the probability to be low as having collisions imposes a performance penalty as well. There is one attack vector here which is called a Hash DoS whereby constructing a lot of hash collisions you can degrade the performance of a service noticeably.
